Qvyon launches MIMIC Core to turn field recordings into robot test cases

Montréal-based Qvyon Technologies launched publicly on November 12 and disclosed $8 million in financing: $6 million in equity and $2 million in venture debt. The round closed in April, so this is a launch and disclosure, not a second new financing round.

BetaKit ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A public launch and funding disclosure

Montréal-based Qvyon Technologies launched publicly on November 12 and disclosed $8 million in financing: $6 million in equity and $2 million in venture debt. The round closed in April, so this is a launch and disclosure, not a second new financing round.

Variations grounded in field data

MIMIC Core takes customer camera, lidar and radar recordings, reconstructs environments in three dimensions and over time, and generates variants for testing weaknesses before deployment. Hosted and self-hosted options include a scenario editor, Python and API access. The company says customer data is not used to train other customers’ models.

Early users and remaining evidence

BetaKit identifies NuPort Robotics and manufacturer Voltava as early customers. The roughly 20-person team plans expansion in the US, Europe and Japan. Detecting failures earlier is the intended benefit; the launch neither certifies customer robots nor supplies independent, quantified proof of risk reduction.
